[documented] s.111A applies to a short-term gain on an equity share or equity-oriented unit on which STT is paid; a short-term gain outside it is charged at the rates applicable to the total income. [documented] Schedule CG is the head-of-income schedule for a capital gain however it is taxed. [inferred] Which specific assets fall outside s.111A — a debt or gold ETF, unlisted shares held short, physical gold — follows from that section text and is not separately notified.

[observed, this engine] Routing the same figure through --other-slab-income must produce identical tax; only the head of income differs. [inferred] That equality is what makes the output usable as a Schedule CG cross-check, which is the reason the flag exists.

[documented] Capital-loss set-off and carry-forward under s.70/71/74 has an ordering, an intra-head restriction and an 8-year carry-forward requiring Schedules CYLA, BFLA and CFL. [observed, this engine] A broker reports a short-term loss as a negative figure, and it reaches slab income where the existing negative special-rate check never sees it.

[documented] ITR-4 carries no Schedule CG, so a capital gain that must be reported there cannot be filed on it whatever the presumptive position or the 50 lakh limit. [inferred] The resulting return for a presumptive filer with such a gain is ITR-3.
